chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abu al-Maghra, from al-Halbi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Every interest (riba) that people consumed due to ignorance, then repented, it is accepted from them if their repentance is recognized from them.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man inherited wealth from his father and knew that there was interest in that wealth, but it had been mixed in trade with other permissible wealth, then the permissible part is permissible and good, so let him consume it; and if he recognizes something from it that is interest, let him take the capital of his wealth and return the interest.'

And whoever man acquired much wealth in which he had increased with interest, and was ignorant of that, then recognized it afterwards, and intended to remove it from what has passed, it is for him, and he should leave it regarding what he resumes.
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim handle inherited wealth that is mixed with interest (riba)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that ignorance of riba in mixed wealth excuses the owner, allowing them to retain the principal and purify the remainder by extracting the interest, whereas those who knowingly accumulate riba must return the excess. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and practical ease (*taysir*) in financial transactions, distinguishing between accidental mixing and deliberate accumulation. The hadith emphasizes that repentance and identification of the interest are key to validating the remaining wealth.
